hypothesis_card.mechanism: Within an AWS instance family (p4d/p5/...), spot prices across AZs share an administered level set by AWS's spot-pricing algorithm; AZ-level deviations are transient capacity artifacts (reclaimed Capacity Blocks, regional demand spikes). Over 90-180 days the below-median AZs converge up (measured on 2023-06..2024-03 pseudo-origins: up-only shift h180 +0.063 / h90 +0.055 skill vs seed, positive in 7/10 origins, and beating both constant uplift +0.027 and the symmetric form), so adding clip(diff, 0, 0.5) * w (w=0.5 at h90, 0.7 at h180) to the seed's pooled 730-day change quantiles reduces the q50/q90 under-forecast on cheap AZs.
hypothesis_card.expected_observation: Discovery pooled skill rises from 0.2450 to ~0.267 (+0.022), with h180 +0.026 and h90 +0.027, h30 unchanged (gated); coverage_80 rises ~+0.022 (fewer q90 breaches on below-median series); median skill +0.017. Dense backtest: pooled +0.022 with z >> 2, ~2/3 of origins improved, helped series concentrated in below-median p4d AZs (use2-az2, apne1-az4, usw2-az3).
hypothesis_card.competing_explanation: The gain is not cross-sectional mean reversion but a generic upward center shift that happens to look good in the 2023-24 AI-demand Discovery window (any uplift would score well while prices rose); alternatively it is pure variance reduction from shrinking the gap to the family median. Evidence against the rival: constant uplift (+0.10/+0.20 log) scored only +0.027 h180 vs up_only's +0.063 on the same pseudo-origins, and the down-only direction was Discovery-NEGATIVE (-0.019 h180, dry run 1) — a generic "prices rose" artifact would have rewarded both directions.
hypothesis_card.test: Paired dry run on the 16 Discovery origins (pooled +0.0225, 10/16 origins improved, h90 +0.027 / h180 +0.026, coverage +0.022) plus a dense 33-origin stride-14 backtest inside Discovery (pooled delta +0.0219, origin-bootstrap SE 0.0027, z = 8.0, 64% of origins improved, helped cells concentrated in below-median p4d AZs, worst regression -0.003 on a single p5 series). The direction was decided by a pseudo-origin scan restricted to the scored window after the down-only variant failed the screen (-0.009 pooled).
hypothesis_card.rejection_condition: Rejected if Discovery pooled skill <= champion (0.2450) or any sanity check fails (final: 0.2675, screen PASS). The reversion hypothesis is falsified if the h90/h180 gains do not transfer out of sample (Holdout h90 <= 0.2150 or h180 <= 0.3551, the champion's values) or if the dense backtest delta is not significant (|z| < 2); measured z = 8.0, so only a Holdout reversal would falsify it.

hypothesis: At 30/90/180-day horizons, AWS GPU spot prices are administered around an instance-family level: AZs priced BELOW their family cross-sectional median level revert UP toward it over 90-180 days (AWS compresses spot discounts and rebalances reclaimed capacity across AZs), so shifting the whole quantile triple of below-median AZs up toward the family median (weight 0.5 at h90, 0.7 at h180, clip 0.5 log) cuts the long-horizon pinball loss that the seed's pure last-value x pooled-change-quantile forecast leaves on the table. Above-median AZs are left untouched (down-shift measured Discovery-negative, -0.019 h180) and h30 is gated off (measured loss-negative).
market_insight: The forecast assumes AWS GPU spot prices over 90-180 days are administered around an instance-family level rather than drifting freely per AZ: AWS actively manages spot pricing to keep it attractive (re:Invent 2024 capacity-management recap, zenn.dev/articles/831696491092b17: "there has been a significant drop [in Spot prices] over the past year. We continue to look for ways to lower these prices further"), and Capacity Blocks for ML (AWS News Blog, 2023-10-31, aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/announcing-amazon-ec2-capacity-blocks-for-ml) reclaim idle GPU capacity so under-used AZs do not stay cheap forever — both forces pull below-median AZs back toward the family median, which is the direction the committed shift encodes. The AI-demand context (NextPlatform 2024-05-02 H100 allocation data; TechSpot 2024-02-27 on easing H100 lead times) supports premium-family (p5) prices staying elevated while older p4d capacity is repriced. The view would change if AWS stopped compressing spot discounts (e.g. a broad spot price INCREASE leaving below-median AZs persistently cheap), if a new generation (p6/Blackwell) made current p5/p4d capacity structurally obsolete and monotonically cheaper, or if the dense backtest's below-median reversion gain failed to transfer to the 2025 Holdout window.
